places.description: A family apartment in an ordinary Sapporo residential district, within walking distance of convenience shops and local streets that require seasonal snow management.
A municipal school setting in Sapporo with ordinary classrooms, a gym or activity space, subject teachers, school routines and seasonal changes to outdoor access.
A combination of walking and Sapporo public transport used for school, errands and cross-city trips, with winter conditions sometimes changing how long ordinary journeys take.
A Sapporo municipal library setting with books, study space, lending and public programming available to children, students and other residents.
A neighborhood commercial area with groceries, convenience shops, small restaurants, pharmacies and repair or household services used for routine errands.

householdShape: Two caregivers, the subject and a younger sibling share an apartment; an older relative lives elsewhere in Sapporo and joins some meals, errands and family visits.
familyRelations: The younger sibling is four years younger than the subject.
The older relative lives separately and remains part of recurring family logistics without being a household member.
materialCircumstances: Housing, food and schooling are generally stable, but the household budgets ordinary expenses and relies on public transport, walking and neighborhood services rather than assuming private-car access for every trip.
mobilityPattern: Walking and public transport are ordinary; winter snow and ice can alter routes, timing and household routines, while snow clearing and road maintenance are visible parts of seasonal city life.
schoolingOrCommunityContext: Municipal schooling, libraries, neighborhood commerce, public transport, sports or cultural activities and seasonal city services create repeated contact with peers and adults outside the household.
culturalContext: Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan — The household lives in Sapporo during 2004–2026. Japanese is the ordinary school and civic language, with English encountered unevenly through school, media and the internet. Cold snowy winters materially affect walking, roads and schedules, while municipal snow removal and snow-processing infrastructure are ordinary public-service facts rather than symbolic lessons. Libraries, schools, neighborhood commerce, public transport, parks, sports, arts, food culture and digital media provide multiple social and intellectual settings. Seasonal festivals and public events may be encountered without assigning the subject an attitude toward them. These facts constrain what can happen; they do not prescribe temperament, values, politics, religion, competence or adult conclusions.
intellectualEnvironment: School curricula, municipal libraries, Japanese and translated books, television and news, internet access, family conversation, museums or cultural programming, practical household knowledge and ordinary disagreement are available unevenly across the chronology.
